alt.en: A light pencil drawing across an open sketchbook page: a church tower with battlements and a weathervane rises among trees on a hill, with a wide valley and low hills beyond. Down the left-hand page is written "Hodnet church. June 1. 1821", and the page is numbered 29 in the top corner. There are no people.
alt.es: Un dibujo a lápiz, suave, sobre la página de un cuaderno de bocetos abierto: una torre de iglesia con almenas y una veleta se alza entre árboles en una colina, con un valle ancho y colinas bajas al fondo. En el margen de la página izquierda está escrito "Hodnet church. June 1. 1821", y la página lleva el número 29 en la esquina de arriba. No hay personas.

caption.en: Hodnet church in Shropshire, sketched on 1 June 1821 by Maria Leycester, in the years when Heber was its rector and wrote his hymns there.
caption.es: La iglesia de Hodnet, en Shropshire, dibujada el 1 de junio de 1821 por Maria Leycester, en los años en que Heber era su rector y escribía allí sus himnos.

source: Maria Leycester (1798 to 1870), Hodnet Church, June 1, 1821, sketchbook leaf 29; graphite, brown wash and watercolour on cream wove paper, 16.2 x 23.8 cm
library: Yale Center for British Art, Prints and Drawings

alt.en: A cream book page numbered 84, headed "TRINITY SUNDAY." and "R. H.", with the hymn's four verses, from "Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty!" to "God in three persons, blessed Trinity!" There is no music.
alt.es: Una página de libro de color crema, numerada 84, con el encabezado "TRINITY SUNDAY." y "R. H.", y las cuatro estrofas del himno, desde "Holy, holy, holy, Lord God Almighty!" hasta "God in three persons, blessed Trinity!" No hay música.

caption.en: Holy, Holy, Holy on page 84 of Heber's Hymns, published by his widow in 1827 and the earliest printing that survives, headed "Trinity Sunday", in four verses and without music.
caption.es: Holy, Holy, Holy en la página 84 de Hymns, el libro de Heber que publicó su viuda en 1827 y la impresión más antigua que se conserva, con el encabezado "Trinity Sunday", en cuatro estrofas y sin música.

source: Reginald Heber, Hymns, Written and Adapted to the Weekly Church Service of the Year (London: John Murray, 1827), p. 84, "Trinity Sunday"
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
callNumber: Princeton Theological Seminary Library SCC; Internet Archive writadap00hebe
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1827; the words are Heber's, who died in 1826. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A page of printed music headed "Trinity Sunday." in Gothic letters and "Hymn 135." Three systems of two staves, with four sharps in the key signature, end with "A-men." Below them is a line from Revelation, "They rest not day and night, saying, Holy, Holy, Holy", and then four verses beginning "HOLY, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty!" There are small pencil marks at the top.
alt.es: Una página de música impresa con el encabezado "Trinity Sunday." en letra gótica y "Hymn 135." Tres sistemas de dos pentagramas, con cuatro sostenidos en la armadura, terminan con "A-men." Debajo hay una línea del Apocalipsis, "They rest not day and night, saying, Holy, Holy, Holy", y después cuatro estrofas que empiezan "HOLY, Holy, Holy! Lord God Almighty!" Arriba hay pequeñas marcas a lápiz.

caption.en: Hymn 135 in the first Hymns Ancient and Modern (1861), under Trinity Sunday: Dykes's new tune, now called NICAEA, in his own harmony, with Revelation 4:8 printed above Heber's words.
caption.es: El himno 135 en la primera edición de Hymns Ancient and Modern (1861), entre los del domingo de la Trinidad: la nueva melodía de Dykes, hoy llamada NICAEA, con su propia armonía y con Apocalipsis 4:8 impreso sobre la letra de Heber.

source: Hymns Ancient and Modern, for use in the services of the Church, with accompanying tunes, musical editor William Henry Monk (London: Novello, 1861), Hymn 135, "Trinity Sunday"
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1861; tune and harmony by John Bacchus Dykes, died 1876; words by Heber, died 1826; musical editor Monk died 1889. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
